title: penstemon clevelandii subsp. connatus
intro: Penstemon clevelandii subsp. connatus, commonly known as the Purple Sage or Cleveland's Penstemon, is a species of flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. This shrubby perennial is native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico, and is valued for its ornamental flowers and potential medicinal properties. The plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including respiratory problems and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of Penstemon clevelandii subsp. connatus include iridoid glycosides, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are believed to contribute to its therapeutic actions of reducing inflammation and fighting off infections.
